html:
The stay of Megasthenes, a Greek envoy from the king Seleucus I, at the court of Chandragupta Maurya in Pataliputra, around 300 BCE.

Seleucus, heir to Alexander's eastern lands, had fought Chandragupta and then made peace around 305 BCE. He handed over lands in the northwest, and Chandragupta gave him 500 war elephants, which helped him win the battle of Ipsus in 301 BCE. Embassies followed, and Megasthenes was one of the envoys of the Seleucid Empire.

He wrote a book about India, the Indica. It is lost, but later writers such as Arrian, Strabo and Diodorus quoted it. He described Pataliputra as a vast city behind wooden walls along the Ganges, the king's court and army, and Indian society divided into seven classes. He also passed on tall stories, such as gold-digging ants. Even so, it was the first Western eyewitness description of India and the main Greek source on the Maurya Empire.
sum: The stay of Megasthenes, a Greek envoy from the king Seleucus I, at the court of Chandragupta Maurya in Pataliputra, around 300 BCE.
